title: The swing with the shortening rope

data.source: Action-angle variables; Noether (1918); adiabatic invariance (Einstein 1911, Ehrenfest 1916). Computed on a harmonic oscillator whose frequency is raised from 1 to 2.

prediction: With the phase read as the angle variable, cuts follow the phase integral; when the frequency is changed slowly the Fisher arc of each half-turn stays put in balanced coordinates (it is pi sqrt(2J)), grows by the ellipse factor in raw coordinates (I first wrote 1.2111; the elliptic integral gives 1.0903), and is not kept under a sudden change.
baseline: Adiabatic invariance of the action J = E / w (Ehrenfest 1916), action-angle variables, and Noether's theorem (1918).
why: Every statement held. Read through action-angle variables, CRR's phase is the angle and its count per half-turn is the square root of the action: the classical adiabatic invariant under another name. In raw position and momentum the same count grew by 9 per cent (I had guessed 21), and R1 (ASSUMPTION) does not say which coordinates to use; Phoenix lists that as OPEN. So the theorem is doing all the work.
